items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: So I ended up on a club date in Connecticut with Lou Stein. So we were in the middle of this gig and we’re just playing dinner music or something.

ctx.x: He was a really good jazz piano player who was active in the 40s, 50s, until maybe twenty years ago, active in New York, played with a lot of people. And one of the 45s that my mother had was the thing that Lou had, it was kind of a fluke hit called “Soft Sands.” And so I remember playing that a lot of times and I memorized the melody and could play it on my horns, on clarinet to begin with. So fast forward, oh God, ‘til the late 1980s and I end up on this club date, by club date I’m using the musician’s term,…
I’ll be darned. That’s a great moment. What about radio? Did it have any impact on you?
